Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Consumer Brands Inc., or GCB, Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for queuing and unmuting will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Emily Carter, Head of Investor Relations.

Emily Carter:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss GCB's Q3 2024 results. With me on the call are Michael Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Rachel Kim, Chief Financial Officer; David Patel, Chief Marketing Officer; and Lisa Chen, Chief Supply Chain Officer; along with other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Michael Thompson.

Michael Thompson:
Thank you, Emily. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. GCB delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment marked by persistent inflation, shifting consumer behaviors, and supply chain volatility, yet remain focused on executing our strategic priorities of premiumization, digital acceleration, and operational excellence.

Our discussion today will cover six key aspects: overall financial performance, brand performance and innovation, supply chain and operational efficiency, marketing and promotional activities, sustainability initiatives, and outlook for the remainder of the year.

I will now turn the call over to Rachel Kim to provide more detail on our financial results.

Rachel Kim:
Thank you, Michael. As Michael mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $11.2 billion, representing a 5.2% increase compared to the prior year on a reported basis and 4.6% on an organic basis, excluding 1.2 percentage points from favorable FX in emerging markets and the impact of divesting our low-margin private-label cleaning line earlier this year. Gross margin expanded to 48.7%, up 220 basis points year-over-year and 90 basis points sequentially, driven by pricing discipline, favorable mix, and supply chain productivity. Operating income reached $2.0 billion, up 8.1%, while diluted earnings per share came in at $1.48. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.

Let me start by unpacking our organic sales growth of 4.6%, which exceeded our guided range of 3% to 4% and marks the fifth straight quarter of positive momentum. This reflects the strength of our core CPG portfolio, including household care like our flagship laundry liquids, personal care staples, and snacks and beverages, even as we contend with softening sentiment in developed markets and rising input costs for commodities such as cocoa, palm oil, and PET resins. Year-to-date, organic sales are up 5.1%, positioning us for full-year growth of 4.5% to 5%, in line with peers like Colgate-Palmolive and Kimberly-Clark.

Breaking it down, pricing contributed 3.2%, through disciplined everyday low pricing on core items and targeted 5-7% increases on premium offerings like our VitalGlow organic skincare and NutriBoost plant-based protein snacks, outpacing broader category CPI inflation of 2.8% per IRI data. Volumes rose 1.8%, powered by share gains in high-growth areas, notably 2.4% in household and personal care from the relaunched EverClean laundry pods, which boosted household penetration 12% with over 1,500 ACV distribution points at Walmart and Kroger. Mix was a slight -0.4% drag from some trade-down in premium beauty, offset by our VitalValue sub-brand.

Regionally, North America, 55% of sales, led with 6.2% organic growth from 4% e-commerce volume—Amazon up 18%—and innovation like our Zestify kombucha capturing 150 basis points in functional beverages. EMEA at 25% of sales grew 2.1%, with 4.8% pricing offsetting a 1.5% volume dip amid UK and German inflation pressures, aided by 100% recycled PET on AquaPure water earning slots at Tesco and Carrefour. Latin America and Asia-Pacific, 20% combined, hit 4.8%, with Brazil beverages up 9% on low-sugar demand and localized flavors like chili-lime NutriBoost in India and Indonesia.

This performance stems from our Velocity 2025 agenda: pruning 15% of low-velocity SKUs to focus on power brands driving 70% of growth, expanding e-commerce to 14% of sales with 25% DTC subscription growth via Shopify, and enhancing supply chain resilience through SAP S/4HANA and AI forecasting to cut stockouts 40%. Sustainability plays in too, with 60% recyclable packaging aligning with EU rules and Gen Z preferences. For Q4, we see 4% to 5% organic growth on seasonal lifts, with mid-single-digit full-year results outpacing industry consensus.

Shifting to gross margin at 48.7%, our best in over five years outside pandemic distortions, this expansion tracks to our full-year 48-49% target. Pricing actions drove about 180 basis points, with 5-7% list increases across Heritage Snacks like NutriCrunch bars and Everyday Essentials beverages passed through effectively—North America AUR up 6.2% versus 3.8% category inflation per IRI. Elasticity held at -2.5x, better than modeled, thanks to premium household penetration.

Favorable mix added 120 basis points, as premium organic beverages grew 15% YoY—8% of sales but 12% of gross profit—while plant-based VitalHarvest proteins at 55%+ margins outshone legacy snacks at 42%. Supply chain productivity contributed 140 basis points via our Enterprise Optimization program across 80% of 45 plants, using AI like Blue Yonder for 12% waste reduction and 8.2x inventory turns, plus a palm oil JV in Indonesia securing 20% of needs 10% below spot amid +25% rallies. Robotics in Ohio and Guadalajara trimmed labor in COGS 8%, with $45 million quarterly savings toward $180 million annually.

Headwinds totaled 220 basis points: 110 from input inflation like dairy +18%, cocoa +45% on crop issues hitting Hershey and Mars peers, PET +12%; 60 from packaging, hedged 70%; and 50 from FX. Regionally, North America hit 52.1% (+310 bps) on snacks and personal care pricing/mix; EMEA 45.3% (+150 bps) despite energy hikes, offset by sustainable sourcing; Asia-Pacific/LatAm 47.9% (+200 bps) from China D2C. This resilience funds 2.5% sales in R&D for stevia-reduced beverages and 30% recycled packaging cutting resin 5-7% while boosting loyalty. Q4 eyes 49.0-49.5%, high end of guide barring cocoa spikes above $4,000/MT or Red Sea drags, mitigated by Mexico nearshoring.

Before moving on, a few words on price elasticity observations, central to our pricing strategy in this inflationary world where unit demand sensitivity to ASP changes balances growth and margins. Our Pricing Center of Excellence uses IRI/Nielsen data and proprietary ML models on 15+ years of POS/e-comm transactions. Portfolio-wide elasticity improved to -0.38 in Q3 from -0.52 prior year and -0.45 Q2—most favorable since 2019 pre-pandemic, versus industry -0.65 per McKinsey, meaning 1% ASP rise yields just 0.38% volume drop amid 3-4% CPI.

By category: Home Care (42% sales) at -0.22 strongest, with +6.8% pricing on fabric care/household cleaners; Tide Ultra Pods equivalent saw +7.2% ASP, -1.5% volumes for 5.6% net revenue per unit, low substitution risk as private label stabilizes at 22% Nielsen, aided by CleanBoost relaunch cutting trade-down 15%; surface cleaners -0.35 from discounters like Aldi. Beauty & Personal Care (28%) -0.15 resilient, +4.9% ASP flat volumes; Olay Regenerist-like serum +5.5% pricing +1.2% volumes on premiumization, 8% trade-up per Circana mirroring P&G SK-II; mass shampoo -0.55 on promotions. Food & Snacks (30%) most elastic -0.62; overall +4.2% ASP but Pringles rival -0.78 on +6.1% pricing from dollar channels/Mondelez; high-protein bars -0.25 gaining 3.5 MMS points amid Ozempic trends.

Regionally: North America (55%) -0.25 best, club packs like Costco -0.12 vs. single-serve -0.45; Europe (20%) -0.48 from energy inflation/Lidl-Aldi at 28% share, UK laundry capped +4%; LatAm/Asia (25%) -0.72 on FX like 15% ARS weaken, Brazil beauty moderated to +2.5% stabilizing -3.1% volumes.

Initiatives include AI Elasticity Engine on Google Cloud/Salesforce predicting 92% accuracy 12 weeks out with 50+ variables for Walmart pilots; micro-testing on DTC/Amazon by income deciles (-0.18 high-income vs. -0.75 value); bundling like Tide-Chips 20% off cutting elasticity 20%, lifting baskets 12%. This Value + Innovation playbook sustains pricing power; Q4 -0.35 to -0.40 supports 4-5% organic, 200bps margin expansion via premium sustainable pods for Gen Z at -0.10.

Market share trends also impress, with 110 basis points overall dollar share gain per Nielsen/IRI—eighth straight quarter under our Premiumize and Digitize strategy. Beauty & Personal Care (35% revenue) +180 bps to 22.4%, NovaGlow serum +4.2 points to 15.8% on hyaluronic clean-beauty launch, +2.3 household penetration, 25% e-comm repeat uplift; mass haircare -50 bps to 18.2% offset by hero SKUs/trial +15%. Home Care (28%) +90 bps to 19.7%, NovaClean pods +2.1 to 21.3% outpacing Tide on 92% ACV/1,200 numeric points via bio-enzyme pods cutting plastic 30%, 18% NPI success; surface steady +60 bps on EDLP at 52% margins. Oral Care (15%) +140 bps to 24.1%, whitening strips +3.5 to 16.2%, +220 bps floss/rinses on bundles +12% baskets. Snacks & Nutrition (22%) +70 bps to 13.8%, NovaFuel bars +2.8 to 9.5% vs. Clif/Kind, +4,500 club points; savory -40 bps offset by air-fried chips 22% trial.

Regions: North America (42%) +130 bps to 21.6%, beauty +210 bps Amazon/Ulta, home +1,800 Walmart SAM; premium skincare 45% mix. EMEA (25%) +90 bps to 18.9%, UK/Germany laundry +150 bps cold-water tech +12 NPS; France oral countered DTC. APAC (20%) +160 bps to 14.2%, China skincare +3.1 Tmall/JD 35% GMV, India snacks +220 Blinkit rural nets; Japan oral 22.5%. LatAm (13%) +80 bps to 16.7%, Brazil home +190 sachets, Mexico beauty 65% tienditas.

Drivers: 22 NPIs 75% hitting 10%+ share fast via $250M AI R&D/SymphonyAI halving forecasts; 15,000 dist points, e-comm 18%; dynamic pricing -2.5 elasticity, divest 5% low-share for premium +8 margins. FY full-year 100+ bps gains via NovaTech 15% savings, $150M DTC/TikTok, plant-based M&A. Gross margin fortress/12-month turns aid.

Supply chain efficiencies and productivity savings fueled 210 bps gross expansion to 48.2%, delivering $185 million YoY or 2.3% sales—third straight sequential gain toward $1B cumulative by 2026, ahead on $520M FY23. Procurement/raws $72M (39%): zero-based locked multi-year vs. palm +18% El Niño/PET +12%, AI SAP Ariba consolidated 15% vendors for 4.2% deflation; regen palm 8% yields/-12% Scope 3; NA $35M Mexico nearshoring, EMAP $22M local sugar/corn. Manufacturing $54M (29%): 92% OEE digital twins Cincinnati/Shanghai -28% downtime, cobots +15% throughput, aseptic ML yields; Europe $18M biomass -22% energy, EMAP $20M India modulars. Logistics $42M (23%): Blue Yonder TMS backhauls -14% NA trucks VMI Walmart/Kroger -30% last-mile; Europe hubs $12M, EMAP $15M drones/cycle -25%. Inventory $17M (9%): AI Nielsen/IRI DOH 52 from 61 unlocking $275M cash, 98.5% service.

Structural via $250M digitization—blockchain 80% palm like Unilever, resilient Red Sea +1% vs. peers 3-5%; sust 6% circular 25% rPET. FY24 another $200M, 60% productivity. Diversified footprint/$100M buffer mitigates palm/geopolitics.

Finally, capex plans: FY24 $450M or 4.2% projected sales, +15% YoY but disciplined vs. P&G/Unilever 5-6%, targeting 15-18% IRRs/payback <4 years across supply chain modernization (45%, $200M), sustainability (30%, $135M), innovation/digital (25%, $115M).

Modernization: automation/digital twins Chicago snacks $45M ABB/Cognex +25% throughput/-15% labor to 92% util; aseptic Mexico/Rotterdam; NA 40%, APAC $60M Vietnam flex cell teas. Sustainability: $50M solar/wind NA 35% Scope 2 offset PepsiCo-style; EMEA $30M Warsaw water 70% recycle; LatAm $20M Brazil biomass -40% gas, $25M annual savings by 2026/Walmart pref. Innovation: $40M Atlanta protein bars 50M units VitalFuel vs. Clif/RXBAR to 18% innov sales; $35M micro-ful DCs SAP/AWS SageMaker DTC/Amazon -3% OOS +bundles. Regional: NA 50%, EMEA 25%, APAC 15%, LatAm 10%; divest EE plants $25M funds. FY25 $460-470M flat+5% more AI maint -20% downtime/precision ferm alt-protein $50B mkt. Underpins mid-teens EPS vs. inflation/private label/China.

With that, I'll turn the call over to David Patel to discuss marketing and brand performance.

David Patel:
Thank you, Rachel. We saw strong performance across our core brands, particularly NovaGlow in premium skincare and NovaClean in laundry, where innovation like hyaluronic clean-beauty and bio-enzyme pods drove double-digit velocity and share gains. Our digital marketing efforts, including TikTok Shop pilots and personalized DTC bundling, are driving significant engagement—e-comm now 18% of sales with 25% repeat uplift—and strong results from our Velocity campaigns emphasizing better-for-you trends. Pricing elasticity insights from Rachel inform targeted promotions, like buy-laundry-get-snacks bundles reducing effective elasticity 20% and lifting basket velocity 12%. We're accelerating premium launches for Gen Z sustainability plays.

Following me, Lisa Chen will provide an update on our supply chain initiatives.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, David. We continue to focus on optimizing our supply chain to improve efficiency and reduce costs, delivering those $185 million savings Rachel highlighted through procurement shielding, 92% OEE smart factories, TMS logistics shifts, and AI inventory discipline. We're implementing new technologies like digital twins, cobots, IoT predictive maintenance, and gen-AI demand sensing across 65% of footprint, enhancing responsiveness to disruptions—Red Sea added just 1% cost via diversified 45% NA/30% Europe/25% EMAP ops and $100M continuity plan. Sustainability infrastructure like solar, water recycling, biomass aligns with regs and saves $25M annually, securing retailer status while funding innovation.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for questions: press star then 1 on your touchtone phone. Our first question comes from Sarah Lee with JPMorgan.

Sarah Lee:
Could you provide more insight into the geographic performance, particularly in emerging markets?

Michael Thompson:
Thanks, Sarah. Absolutely, emerging markets remain a high-growth engine, contributing 25% to sales with organic growth of 4.8%. In Asia-Pacific, China skincare surged on Tmall/JD platforms with NovaGlow K-beauty essences driving 35% GMV, while India snacks gained via Blinkit quick-commerce and rural micro-networks like Project Shakti. Latin America saw Brazil home care +190 bps share with affordable sachets and beverages +9% on urban low-sugar demand despite ARS volatility—we moderated beauty pricing to +2.5% stabilizing volumes. Elasticity here at -0.72 reflects FX pressures, but localized sourcing and nearshoring mitigate. Overall, EMs outpaced developed with innovation and dist mastery.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Ross with Goldman Sachs.

Mike Ross:
How are you managing inventory levels given the current economic uncertainty?

Rachel Kim:
Good question, Mike. Inventory discipline is key, with days on hand down to 52 from 61 via gen-AI on 36 months Nielsen/IRI data, unlocking $275M cash without stockouts—service at 98.5% despite 8% category growth. We've reduced safety stocks on seasonal like BBQ sauces, fine-tuned forecasting with SAP S/4HANA cutting stockouts 40%, and leveraged VMI pilots with Walmart/Kroger for D2SD -30% last-mile. In uncertainty, this agility supports volume resilience while funding capex priorities like micro-fulfillment for e-comm surge.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Anna Patel with Barclays.

Anna Patel:
Can you discuss the progress on your sustainability goals and any related cost implications?

Lisa Chen:
Thanks, Anna. Sustainability is core, with $135M capex this year on solar/wind offsetting 35% Scope 2 by 2026, Warsaw water recycling 70%, Brazil biomass -40% gas dependency—projected $25M annual savings, already securing Walmart/Carrefour status. Circular packaging at 25-30% recycled PET cuts resin 5-7%, contributes 6% to productivity savings, aligns EU Deforestation/U.S. SEC rules, and boosts loyalty—Gen Z 28-35% premium pay per NielsenIQ. ROIC-positive, no margin drag; enhances resilience like regen palm 8% yields/-12% Scope 3.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Rivera with Morgan Stanley.

Tom Rivera:
What are your expectations for pricing elasticity in the coming quarters?

David Patel:
Hi Tom. Building on Rachel's details, we expect Q4 elasticity at -0.35 to -0.40 portfolio-wide, supporting 4-5% organic and 200bps margin expansion. Category variances persist—home care -0.22 resilient, snacks -0.62 elastic—but AI engine 92% accurate forecasts, micro-tests by income, and bundling sharpen tactics. Premium sustainable launches target Gen Z -0.10, monitoring tariffs/private label. Our brand equity turns headwinds to tailwinds.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Michael Thompson for closing remarks.

Michael Thompson:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your insightful questions. We remain committed to delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders through disciplined execution on growth, margins, and innovation. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Emily Carter:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Global Consumer Brands Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
